statement: Full-gate runs no longer risk SIGSEGV from raft-logic worker teardown: the dependency stops workers by awaited self-exit (terminate only as bounded-timeout fallback) and this repo consumes that release.

notes.fault: full-gate run 32630984274 (2026-08-23, head 160e439fa): test/raft/spike/raft-logic-spike-cluster.test.js - all assertions passed, then 'test process received SIGSEGV; test process exited without a status' during cluster.stop(). Not reproducible locally (5/5 pass on fast hardware). First observed occurrence; earlier red gates died before sampling this test.
notes.mechanism: raft-logic@0.3.14 raft-worker-controller.mjs stop(): after the graceful 'stop' request resolves it unconditionally calls worker.terminate(). Worker-side ordering is correct (storage.close() before respond), but forcibly terminating a worker thread in a process with a native addon loaded (better-sqlite3) is the documented terminate-vs-native crash class; slow/jittery VMs widen the window. Three ThreadedRaftNodes share the test process, so any worker segfault kills the whole TAP child.
notes.fixSketch: Upstream in codeberg.org/psvensson/raft-logic: after graceful stop response, ask the worker to self-exit (postMessage exit / worker returns from its message loop) and await the 'exit' event with a bounded timeout; call terminate() only on timeout fallback. Then bump the dependency here. Owner of the interaction: controller.stop() owns the whole worker lifecycle end; no caller-side workaround in this repo (a monkey-patch would be a second form of the same logic).
notes.steering: docs/steering/testing-guidelines/harness.md Runner Stability Boundary Policy applies: shared runner-boundary concern, fix at the shared seam (the dependency), not per-suite.

constraints.statement: If this Quest changes source code, spawn a subagent verifier before audit and git handoff, then record a Solver finding with evidence subagent:<id>.
The behavioral fix lands in raft-logic upstream; this repo's bounded change is the dependency bump plus any spike-adapter contract adjustment. No caller-side termination workaround.
